newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Peters sees deal lasting more than three yrs.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Peters sees deal lasting more than three yrs.

text.p: Nationalist New Zealand First leader Winston Peters said on Tuesday he was confident a coalition government would be formed from the talks currently underway, and that an agreement would last more than three years.
"Yes we are confident, but we can't be certain we'll get one (a coalition agreement)," Peters said.
"We are still very confident of effecting an agreement with one or other parties that will last, and more than three years.
"We are interested in establishing a government that has a long life in New Zealand politics."
He said at the next election each party would seek its own market share.

"But it tends to last more than three years because having been out into the constituency and got a public verdict on how you have gone and perhaps how your coalition partner has gone, you would expect to be back in government, surely with a renegotiated agreement depending on your success at the polls, but one which has a precedent set at this point in time.
"That is why this precedent is important for us," Peters told Reuters.
He said the negotiation process would be much more abbreviated next time.

NZ First holds the balance of power after the October 12 election and is negotiating separately with both the conservative National Party and the centre-left Labour Party over the shape of the next government.
Peters has said his preference is for a coalition government but has listed minority Labour and National government as other possible outcomes.
After a round of informal talks with National on Tuesday Peters said he could not predict when the talks would conclude.
"I can't predict...because it is dependent on other parties as well. Sometime in the near future," Peters said.
He said deals with National and Labour would be considered almost simultaneously by the NZ First caucus and he expected it to take two days for the caucus to make a decision.
"To be fair to them and to be fair to the subject matter you are talking two days," Peters said.
He said the NZ First caucus would be in Wellington all week and could be convened quickly.
